symptom_risk_mapping.description: Maps dataset features to their clinical risk relationships with lung cancer

features.name: SMOKING
features.clinical_notes: Strongest single risk factor. 85% of lung cancers are attributable to smoking. Risk increases with pack-years.

features.name: COUGHING
features.clinical_notes: Persistent cough (>3 weeks) is the most common presenting symptom. New or changed cough is significant.

features.name: SHORTNESS_OF_BREATH
features.clinical_notes: Dyspnea may be caused by tumor obstruction, pleural effusion, or lymphangitic spread.

features.name: WHEEZING
features.clinical_notes: Localized wheezing may indicate partial airway obstruction by tumor.

features.name: CHEST_PAIN
features.clinical_notes: Dull, persistent pain suggests pleural or chest wall involvement. Sharp pain may indicate pleuritis.

features.name: SWALLOWING_DIFFICULTY
features.clinical_notes: May indicate mediastinal lymph node enlargement or esophageal compression.

features.name: FATIGUE
features.clinical_notes: Generalized fatigue is common in cancer patients. May be early or late symptom.

features.name: YELLOW_FINGERS
features.clinical_notes: Nicotine staining of fingers. Indicator of heavy smoking rather than direct cancer sign.

features.name: ALCOHOL_CONSUMING
features.clinical_notes: Synergistic effect with smoking. Alone, alcohol is a weak risk factor for lung cancer.

features.name: ANXIETY
features.clinical_notes: May affect symptom reporting accuracy. Not a direct risk factor.

features.name: ALLERGY
features.clinical_notes: Some studies suggest allergies may be inversely related to cancer risk. Complicates differential diagnosis.

features.name: CHRONIC_DISEASE
features.clinical_notes: COPD, pulmonary fibrosis, and other chronic lung diseases increase lung cancer risk.

features.name: PEER_PRESSURE
features.clinical_notes: Social factor. May correlate with smoking initiation.

features.name: AGE
features.clinical_notes: Risk increases exponentially after age 40. Median age at diagnosis is 70 years.

features.name: GENDER
features.clinical_notes: In Turkey, male incidence (ASR 68.0) is significantly higher than female. Primarily due to higher smoking rates.
